# British American Tobacco (BTI) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 033 | Published 2020-09-13 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-9-13/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/033.json)

A defensive fiscal view accompanies tobacco value.

BTI eventually delivered favorable long-window returns, dividends and resumed buybacks, while its acquisition and sanctions risks materialized. The short-horizon fiscal outlook was less precise: breakevens recovered before new legislation. The option discussion contains an assignment error and does not disclose executed contract results.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 033-C01

**Jobs recovery slows after rebound**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | following recovery |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US jobs |
| Source blocks | 5, 8, 10, 13, 14, 18, 19 |
| Thesis family | covid-jobs-slow-recovery |

Hiring slowed after the reopening burst and full payroll recovery took until July 2022. Stagnation overstates continued positive hiring, but the stated fast-partial-then-slow shape is supported.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: following recovery

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [July 2020 employment situation](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072020.htm) | BLS | 2020-08-07 | Verified in the audit

Payrolls rose 1.8 m in July after 4.8 m in June and 2.7 m in May; unemployment fell to 10.2%. Permanent job losers were approximately unchanged at 2.9 m in July; temporary layoffs fell 1.3 m.

- [July 2022 Employment Situation release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08052022.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2022-08-05 | Verified in the audit

The release reported payroll employment and unemployment rate had returned to February 2020 levels in July 2022. This is a publication-vintage recovery date, not a claim about subsequently revised payroll history.

### 033-C02

| --- | --- |

| Asset or variable | US benefits |

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

- [FY 2022 budget results](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy1043) | US Treasury | 2022-10-21 | Verified in the audit

FY 2021 deficit was $2.776 tn/12.3% GDP; FY 2022 $1.375 tn/5.5%. Receipts rose from $4.046 tn to $4.896 tn.

- [June 2022 Consumer Price Index](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_07132022.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2022-07-13 | Verified in the audit

- [July 2023 FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20230726a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2023-07-26 | Verified in the audit

Federal funds target increased to 5.25-5.50%; Treasury/MBS holdings continued to decline. This was tightening rather than a permanent low-rate cap.

### 033-C05

**Disinflation lasts until renewed stimulus**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | until next fiscal package |
| Conditions | Not specified |

Ten-year breakevens fell into September, then exceeded August levels by December 23, before the major package became law. Policy expectations may lead passage; the market is not a contemporaneous on/off fiscal switch.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: until next fiscal package

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Ten-year inflation compensation sensitivity](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFII10) | Federal Reserve via FRED | Verified in the audit

DGS 10 minus DFII 10: August 31, 2020 1.80%, September 14 1.65%, September 25 1.58%, December 23 1.97%. Breakeven includes inflation-risk and liquidity premia, not pure expected CPI.

- [CARES and Consolidated Appropriations Acts](https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/coronavirus/about-the-cares-act) | US Treasury | Verified in the audit

The subsequent broad relief act passed Congress December 21 and was signed December 27, 2020, after the election rather than during summer.

### 033-C10

**Strike crossing guarantees put assignment**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Options |
| Source blocks | 58 |
| Thesis family | american-put-assignment |

American exercise is chosen by the holder; touching or crossing a strike does not automatically assign the seller before expiry. Assignment, exercise-by-exception and contrary instructions must be distinguished.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Options assignment FAQ](https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/options-assignment) | Options Industry Council / OCC | Verified in the audit

American-style exercise is the holder's decision before expiration. At expiration, exercise-by-exception thresholds and contrary instructions apply; going in the money does not itself compel early assignment.
